original_question: For the tree of shifted standard Young tableaux ordered by containment, determine whether the identity is the only automorphism of the underlying unlabeled tree and whether each node is uniquely determined by the sequence of rank sizes in the subtree rooted at that node.
target_in_paper: Section 1 ("Problems of 2024"), Open Problem 2: the open problem on the tree SSYT of shifted standard Young tableaux under containment.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the two substantive parts of the paper's formulation almost verbatim: (i) the question whether the underlying unlabeled tree of shifted standard Young tableaux has only the identity automorphism, and (ii) the question whether a node is uniquely determined by the rank-cardinality data of the subtree rooted at that node. It also correctly identifies containment as the source of the tree structure.
missing_details: The paper treats this as an open problem motivated by computation: it says computation suggests both properties, rather than stating them as established facts.

To be fully stand-alone, the tree should be defined explicitly as the rooted containment tree on all shifted standard Young tableaux, typically with the empty tableau as root and edges corresponding to adding one new maximal entry (equivalently, containment with size difference 1).

The phrase "underlying unlabeled tree" should be made explicit as meaning the abstract graph obtained from this rooted tree, with automorphisms taken in the graph-theoretic sense and not as shape-preserving or label-preserving tableau maps.

The phrase "sequence of rank sizes" should be spelled out as the census of the ranks of the rooted subtree: for each depth d >= 0, the number of descendants of the given node lying at distance d from it.
The paper's wording is about each node of the tree, i.e. each individual shifted standard Young tableau, not merely each shifted shape.
refined_question: Let SSYT be the rooted tree whose vertices are all shifted standard Young tableaux (including the empty tableau), where T is adjacent to U when T is contained in U and |U| = |T| + 1; equivalently, U is obtained from T by adding one new largest entry. For a vertex T and each d >= 0, let r_d(T) denote the number of vertices in the subtree rooted at T that lie at distance d from T. Determine whether every automorphism of the abstract underlying unlabeled tree SSYT is the identity, and whether the map T -> (r_0(T), r_1(T), r_2(T), ...) is injective; that is, whether each shifted standard Young tableau is uniquely determined by the census of rank sizes of its rooted subtree.
justification: The draft is aiming directly at Open Problem 2, whose wording is already very close to your draft. The refined version stays narrow by preserving the exact two questions asked there and only making implicit combinatorial conventions explicit: what the containment tree is, what an unlabeled-tree automorphism means, and what the subtree rank census records. The neighboring Open Problem 3 shows that the author is intentionally contrasting the shifted case with the unshifted case, where nontrivial automorphisms are expected, so the question should not be broadened into a general classification of tableau-tree automorphisms. The paper is a notebook of open problems rather than a theorem-proof article, so there is no nearer theorem/proposition reformulation to prefer here.
